title: PaperBench: Evaluating AI's Ability to Replicate AI Research
authors_zh: Giulio Starace, Oliver Jaffe, Dane Sherburn, James Aung, Jun Shern Chan, Leon Maksin, Rachel Dias, Evan Mays, Benjamin Kinsella, Wyatt Thompson, Johannes Heidecke, Amelia Glaese, Tejal Patwardhan
paper_type_zh: 长时程科研智能体复现实验基准与分层验证
best_for_zh: 关注科研智能体、代码执行、分层评分、轨迹发布边界、裁判可靠性与可回放审计的读者
one_line: PaperBench evaluates 20 from-scratch ML-paper replications with 8,316 weighted rubric leaves, fresh-container execution, and an o3-mini judge, but releases no complete 646-run trajectory/submission corpus and remains exposed to judge, contamination, rights, replay, and secret-handling risks.
PaperBench 以 20 篇机器学习论文、8,316 个加权 rubric 叶节点和新鲜容器复现评估科研智能体，但官方并未发布覆盖 646 次论文实验的完整日志、快照、提交物、执行产物与逐叶裁判输出。
why: It turns an open-ended research-replication episode into auditable Code Development, Execution, and Result Match checkpoints and separates agent work from clean reproduction. That same design shows why public task/rubric packages are evaluation assets, not automatically trajectory-training data: the actual rollouts are absent, result reproduction remains near zero, and judge/replay/ contamination/security boundaries materially affect any claimed capability.
inclusion_reason: PaperBench defines a high-value long-horizon research-agent episode around a hidden paper-replication task, code repository, fresh-container execution, and 8,316 author-approved leaf criteria. Its three-stage feedback contract is unusually granular, while absent trajectories, weak Result Match performance, judge/file-selection dependence, contamination, rights, secret exposure, and replay gaps are central reuse boundaries for the Atlas.

title: Problem
问题
html:
PaperBench, formally published at ICML 2025 in PMLR 267, asks whether an AI agent can reproduce the empirical contribution of a machine-learning paper from scratch. Its evaluation set contains 20 ICML 2024 Spotlight or Oral papers. A task bundles the source paper, author addendum, assets, blacklist, configuration, and a hidden hierarchical rubric; a run should additionally produce the tool-use log, repository snapshots, a submission, fresh-container execution evidence, monitor outcome, and leaf-level grades.

The central counting distinction is essential: 8,316 denotes rubric leaves across the 20 papers, divided into 3,674 Code Development, 4,076 Execution, and 566 Result Match leaves. It is not a trajectory count. The paper separately reports 646 experimental runs. Consequently, the public benchmark can support task-level evaluation even though it does not expose a complete run-level corpus suitable for trajectory analysis or training.

PaperBench 正式发表于 ICML 2025，并收录于 PMLR 267；它考察人工智能智能体能否从零复现一篇机器学习论文的实证贡献。评测集包含 20 篇 ICML 2024 Spotlight 或 Oral 论文。每个任务把原论文、作者补充说明、资产、黑名单、配置和隐藏的分层 rubric 组织在一起；一次运行理论上还会产生工具调用日志、代码仓库快照、提交物、新鲜容器执行证据、监控结果和逐叶评分。

最关键的计数边界必须明确：8,316 表示 20 篇论文上的 rubric 叶节点总数，其中 Code Development 为 3,674 个、Execution 为 4,076 个、Result Match 为 566 个；它不是轨迹数量。论文另行报告了 646 次实验运行。因此，公开基准能够支持任务级评测，却没有暴露可直接用于轨迹分析或训练的完整运行级语料。

title: Core idea
核心思路
html:
The benchmark separates an open-ended replication into 3 stages: agent work in an isolated rollout container, execution of the selected submission in a fresh reproduction container, and rubric grading in the judge context. The candidate sees the paper and author addendum but not the rubric or judge-only notes. It must build a submission repository whose reproduction script regenerates the evidence needed for assessment.

Before reproduction, a URL monitor may disqualify a run. SimpleJudge then assigns each rubric leaf a binary 0/1 decision, explanation, and validity flag, after which sibling-relative weights produce parent scores and the final Replication Score. The agent receives no online rubric reward during its episode. This design yields a post-hoc verifier contract, but Result Match has only 566 of 8,316 leaves, so the score is structurally dominated by Code Development and Execution rather than direct agreement with the paper's findings.

该基准把开放式论文复现拆成 3 个阶段：智能体在隔离 rollout 容器中工作、在新鲜复现容器中执行选定提交物、最后在裁判上下文中按 rubric 评分。候选智能体能看到论文和作者补充说明，却看不到 rubric 与仅供裁判使用的说明；它必须构建一个提交仓库，并让其中的复现脚本重新生成评分所需证据。

复现之前，URL 监控器可以判定运行违规。随后 SimpleJudge 对每个叶节点给出二元 0/1 结论、解释和有效性标记，再按同级相对权重聚合父节点与最终 Replication Score。智能体在运行期间不会收到在线 rubric 奖励。这是一种事后验证契约，但 Result Match 仅占 8,316 个叶节点中的 566 个，因此总分在结构上更受 Code Development 与 Execution 支配，而不是主要反映与原论文结论的一致程度。

title: Method
方法
html:
The construction pipeline filtered candidate ICML papers for empirical substance, single-machine feasibility, accessible dependencies, and from-scratch reproducibility. The team contacted 42 author groups and retained 20 papers whose authors agreed to help refine rubrics and addenda. The main comparison targeted 6 models, 20 papers, and 3 runs per pair, while additional IterativeAgent, extended-budget, and human conditions contributed to the reported total.

Each main rollout received up to 12 hours in Ubuntu 24.04 with 1 A10 GPU, Internet access, and optional credentials. The required submission contains a reproduction script and generated results, plots, tables, and logs. Reproduction receives another 12 hours in a fresh container; one extended o1 condition ran for 36 hours. Grading uses o3-mini-2025-01-31. If a submission exceeds judge context, model-based relevance ranking selects only the top 10 files, creating an information bottleneck. The blacklist monitor searches recorded logs for normalized URLs near selected download commands, rather than enforcing a complete network policy.

构建流程先按实证工作量、单机可行性、依赖可获得性和从零复现可能性筛选 ICML 候选论文。团队联系了 42 个作者组，最终保留 20 篇作者同意协助完善 rubric 与补充说明的论文。主比较计划覆盖 6 个模型、20 篇论文以及每个模型—论文组合 3 次运行；另有 IterativeAgent、延长预算和人类条件，共同构成论文报告的运行总量。

每次主 rollout 最多在 Ubuntu 24.04 环境中运行 12 小时，使用 1 张 A10 GPU、互联网连接和可选凭据。提交物必须包含复现脚本，以及生成的结果、图、表和日志；随后在新鲜容器中另给 12 小时执行复现，其中一个扩展 o1 条件运行 36 小时。评分模型是 o3-mini-2025-01-31。若提交物超出裁判上下文，模型相关性排序只保留 top 10 文件，形成信息瓶颈。黑名单监控器仅在记录日志中搜索靠近特定下载命令的规范化 URL，并非完整网络策略。

title: Evidence
证据
html:
Across 646 reported runs, the strongest BasicAgent configuration, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, scores 21.0% ±0.8 on the 20-paper benchmark. IterativeAgent with o1 reaches 24.4% ±0.7 at 12 hours and 26.0% ±0.3 at 36 hours. The same o1 family reaches 43.4% ±0.8 on Code Development. On a 3-paper subset, best-of-3 human participants reach 41.4% after 48 hours, versus 26.6% for o1.

These aggregates do not imply successful result reproduction. Result Match represents only 566 of 8,316 leaves, and reported configurations obtain about 0–1.4% on Result Analysis leaves. JudgeEval includes only 5 manually graded submissions; the selected judge reports F1 0.83 at an estimated $66 per paper. Finally, 10 of 646 runs accessed blacklisted resources and were disqualified. The results therefore support a difficult evaluation finding, not a claim that the released repository contains the evidence objects behind every score.

在论文报告的 646 次运行中，最强 BasicAgent 配置 Claude 3.5 Sonnet 在 20 篇论文基准上得到 21.0% ±0.8。采用 o1 的 IterativeAgent 在 12 小时条件下达到 24.4% ±0.7，在 36 小时条件下达到 26.0% ±0.3；同一 o1 系列在 Code Development 上达到 43.4% ±0.8。在一个 3 篇论文子集上，best-of-3 人类参与者经过 48 小时达到 41.4%，而 o1 为 26.6%。

这些聚合分数并不等于成功复现实验结果。Result Match 只占 8,316 个叶节点中的 566 个，已报告配置在 Result Analysis 叶节点上约为 0–1.4%。JudgeEval 仅包含 5 个手工评分提交物；所选裁判报告 F1 0.83，估算成本为每篇 $66。另有 646 次运行中的 10 次访问黑名单资源而被判零。因此，证据支持“任务很难”的评测结论，却不能证明公开仓库保存了每个分数背后的全部证据对象。

title: Novelty
新意
html:
PaperBench's main contribution is an end-to-end, auditable decomposition of research replication. It links a paper-specific task package to an executable repository, a clean reproduction pass, an author-reviewed weighted rubric, and per-leaf model judgment. The 3-stage isolation makes a useful distinction between code that merely exists and evidence that can be regenerated, while the blacklist check attempts to preserve from-scratch conditions.

The benchmark is also unusually explicit about multiple grading dimensions: 8,316 leaves over 20 papers encode implementation, execution, and result agreement. Yet this richness belongs to the evaluation contract, not to a released trajectory dataset. The paper reports 646 runs, but the repository does not publish their complete interaction histories and artifacts. For an atlas of reasoning data, that distinction is itself novel and important: task packaging, verifier code, and run-level supervision are different release objects with different reuse claims.

PaperBench 的主要贡献，是把科研论文复现分解为一条端到端、可审计的流程。它把论文专属任务包与可执行代码仓库、新鲜容器复现、经作者审阅的加权 rubric 和逐叶模型裁判连接起来。3 阶段隔离清楚地区分了“代码已经存在”和“证据能够重新生成”，黑名单检查则试图维持从零复现条件。

该基准还对多种评分维度做了较细表达：20 篇论文上的 8,316 个叶节点分别覆盖实现、执行和结果一致性。然而，这种丰富性属于评测契约，并不等于已经发布轨迹数据集。论文报告了 646 次运行，但仓库没有公开其完整交互历史和工件。对于推理数据图谱，这一区分本身很重要：任务封装、验证器代码和运行级监督是不同的发布对象，对应的复用主张也不同。

title: Limitations
局限
html:
• Missing run corpus. The paper reports 646 runs, but complete logs, snapshots, submissions, executed artifacts, reproduction records, and leaf-level judge outputs are not released.
  • Rubric imbalance. Of 8,316 leaves, 3,674 cover Code Development, 4,076 Execution, and only 566 Result Match; direct result agreement has a low share.
  • Judge bottlenecks. JudgeEval has only 5 submissions and reports F1 0.83; over-context submissions are reduced to the top 10 ranked files, and both ranking and judgment can drift.
  • Monitor gaps. The blacklist check found 10 violations among 646 runs, but browser access, Python clients, mirrors, indirect downloads, missing logs, or memorized code can evade URL-pattern inspection.
  • Split and contamination drift. The ICML paper describes 2 development papers, while the current public dev split has 3; public papers, rubrics, and judge code also invite future tuning contamination.
  • Replay limits. Ubuntu 24.04 tags are not digest-pinned, and current fallback may use Python 3.11; dependencies, external services, credentials, hardware, seeds, and nondeterministic judges can change.
  • Security and rights. Unproxied network access and up to $1,000 in API credit expose credential and supply-chain risks. The MIT code license does not establish uniform rights for bundled papers, assets, upstream data or models, generated outputs, or all JudgeEval submissions.

• 运行语料缺失。 论文报告 646 次运行，但完整日志、快照、提交物、执行产物、复现记录和逐叶裁判输出均未公开。
  • Rubric 失衡。 8,316 个叶节点中，Code Development 占 3,674 个，Execution 占 4,076 个，Result Match 仅 566 个；直接结果一致性的占比较低。
  • 裁判瓶颈。 JudgeEval 只有 5 个提交物并报告 F1 0.83；超出上下文的提交物仅保留排序后的 top 10 文件，而排序与评分都可能漂移。
  • 监控缺口。 黑名单检查在 646 次运行中发现 10 次违规，但浏览器访问、Python 客户端、镜像、间接下载、缺失日志或记忆代码都可能绕过 URL 模式检查。
  • 划分与污染漂移。 ICML 论文描述 2 篇开发论文，当前公开 dev 划分却有 3 篇；公开论文、rubric 和裁判代码还会带来未来针对性调优污染。
  • 回放受限。 Ubuntu 24.04 标签没有固定摘要，当前兜底流程可能使用 Python 3.11；依赖、外部服务、凭据、硬件、随机种子和非确定裁判都可能变化。
  • 安全与权利。 非代理网络访问和最高 $1,000 API 额度带来凭据与供应链风险。MIT 代码许可不能统一覆盖打包论文、资产、上游数据或模型、生成输出以及全部 JudgeEval 提交物的权利。

title: Usefulness
用途
html:
PaperBench is directly useful for evaluation and audit of long-horizon research agents: the public release provides 20 evaluation task packages, a current 3-paper dev split, rubrics, addenda, assets, blacklists, container and orchestration code, judge and monitor implementations, and a 5-example JudgeEval. These materials support reproducing the benchmark interface, studying verifier design, and diagnosing whether an agent can turn a paper into executable evidence.

It should not be represented as an off-the-shelf SFT or RL trajectory source. The complete 646-run corpus is absent, including failed and disqualified cases, and the public rubric would contaminate any future evaluation if used as a training target. Training reuse would first require run-level artifacts, immutable lineage, rights clearance, secret redaction, stable replay manifests, and stronger judge calibration. Under current evidence, the defensible training-use labels are evaluation and audit only.

PaperBench 直接适合长时程科研智能体的评测与审计：公开版本提供 20 个评测任务包、当前 3 篇论文的 dev 划分、rubric、补充说明、资产、黑名单、容器与编排代码、裁判与监控实现，以及包含 5 个样例的 JudgeEval。这些材料可用于重建基准接口、研究验证器设计，并诊断智能体能否把论文转化为可执行证据。

它不应被描述成可直接用于 SFT 或 RL 的现成轨迹来源。完整的 646 次运行语料并未公开，其中包括失败和被取消资格的案例；若把公开 rubric 当作训练目标，还会污染后续评测。要支持训练复用，首先需要运行级工件、不可变血缘、权利核验、凭据脱敏、稳定回放清单和更强的裁判校准。按当前证据，可辩护的 training-use 仅是 evaluation 与 audit。

title: Reading notes
阅读笔记
html:
• Start with the ICML 2025 / PMLR 267 paper and appendices, then inspect the pinned frontier-evals commit rather than assuming the current main branch matches the publication.
  • Keep 8,316 rubric leaves separate from 646 runs. The former is annotation structure over 20 papers; the latter is an experimental count whose complete artifacts are unavailable.
  • Read the release by object class: 20 evaluation tasks, the current 3 development tasks, rubrics and runner/judge/monitor code are public; full run logs and outputs are not.
  • Inspect the Result Match category before interpreting the aggregate score: it contains only 566 leaves, and the reported Result Analysis scores are about 0–1.4%.
  • Treat JudgeEval's 5 submissions, F1 0.83, and top 10 file selection as limited calibration evidence, not a universal guarantee of grading validity.
  • Track protocol drift explicitly: the paper says 2 dev papers but the current split has 3, while network, credentials, dependencies, retry behavior, licenses, and missing artifacts all constrain replay.

• 先阅读 ICML 2025 / PMLR 267 正式论文及附录，再检查固定的 frontier-evals 提交，不要默认当前 main 分支与论文发布时完全一致。
  • 严格区分 8,316 个 rubric 叶节点与 646 次运行：前者是覆盖 20 篇论文的标注结构，后者是实验计数，而其完整工件不可获得。
  • 按对象类别阅读发布边界：20 个评测任务、当前 3 个开发任务、rubric 以及 runner、judge、monitor 代码公开；完整运行日志与输出未公开。
  • 解读聚合分数前先看 Result Match：该类别仅有 566 个叶节点，报告的 Result Analysis 分数约为 0–1.4%。
  • 将 JudgeEval 的 5 个提交物、F1 0.83 和 top 10 文件选择视为有限校准证据，而非评分有效性的普遍保证。
  • 明确记录协议漂移：论文称有 2 篇 dev 论文，当前划分却有 3 篇；网络、凭据、依赖、重试行为、许可和缺失工件也共同限制回放。

value.html: Twenty ICML 2024 Spotlight and Oral papers were filtered for substantial empirical content, single-machine feasibility, accessible dependencies, no closed-model dependency or new human-data collection, and from-scratch reproducibility. The remaining pool was randomly sampled, then authors were contacted until 20 agreed to co-develop rubrics and addenda.

An Ubuntu 24.04 agent container with one A10 GPU in the reported experiments, the paper and addendum, a writable Git submission repository, shell/Python/ browser/file-reader tools, Internet access, and optional OpenAI/Hugging Face credentials. The hidden rubric is not shown to the candidate.

Tool outputs, file contents, browser results, command results, model/API errors, and elapsed-time state available to the agent; post-rollout records additionally include logs, monitor matches, reproduction logs, file listings, Git history/status, timeout state, and judge explanations.

A self-contained code repository rooted at submission/ with a required reproduce.sh. Executing that script should regenerate the paper's empirical evidence and leave results, plots, tables, and reproduce.log for grading.
The latest or time-targeted submission snapshot and, after execution in a fresh reproduction container, an archived executed submission containing source, script, log, and generated evidence.

The evaluated model plus scaffold produces its own long-horizon tool-use episode. Paper baselines use BasicAgent or IterativeAgent with GPT-4o, o1, o3-mini, DeepSeek-R1, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, or Gemini 2.0 Flash. Complete paper-run episodes and submissions are not released in the official repo.

A ReAct-style sequence of model messages and shell, Python, web-browser, and paginated-file-reader actions that reads the paper, writes code, installs dependencies, runs experiments, troubleshoots, and produces snapshots. IterativeAgent removes voluntary termination and repeatedly asks for the next step; BasicAgent may terminate early.

value.html: Three isolated stages: agent rollout container, fresh reproduction container, and judge execution context. The reported paper uses Ubuntu 24.04 and A10 GPUs for rollout/reproduction, permits Internet access, caps agent work at 12 hours for main experiments and reproduce.sh at 12 hours, and grades reproduced artifacts with o3-mini-2025-01-31 at high reasoning effort.

SimpleJudge returns a binary score, explanation, and valid-score flag for every leaf; the release serializes the graded task tree, scalar score, invalid leaf count, model configuration, timestamp, and token usage. A post-hoc URL monitor can instead disqualify a run to zero before reproduction and judging.

Post-hoc evaluation reward only. Each leaf is 0/1, parent scores are weighted averages of their children, the root is the submission Replication Score, and the headline metric is the mean root score over 20 papers. The agent does not receive rubric rewards during its rollout.

The scaffold terminates voluntarily or reaches its time/step limit; the latest snapshot is selected. Missing snapshots or blacklist violations yield zero. A missing reproduce.sh forces Execution and Result Match leaves to zero but can still leave Code Development credit; reproduction timeouts preserve and grade partial executed state when available. Full replication means every weighted leaf requirement is satisfied.

The repository releases the 20 evaluation task packages, three current dev paper packages, rubrics, addenda, assets, blacklists, split files, Dockerfiles, orchestration/reproduction/judge/monitor code, and a five-example JudgeEval with manual leaf labels. It does not release the 646 paper-result runs as a complete corpus of agent logs, snapshots, submissions, executed artifacts, reproduction records, or per-leaf judge outputs.

ICML paper pool -> automated and manual suitability filtering -> random selection plus author participation -> engineer-drafted, internally reviewed, author-approved rubric/addendum -> hidden-rubric agent rollout -> snapshot -> blacklist-log monitor -> fresh-container reproduction -> per-leaf LLM judgment -> weighted score and run aggregation.

Two research engineers draft each rubric; internal reviewers and one or more original paper authors iteratively verify it and supply clarifications. The evaluated base model then generates the rollout and repository. SimpleJudge supplies post-hoc grades, not trajectory demonstrations.

Selected ICML 2024 Spotlight/Oral papers, paper Markdown/PDF, original-author addenda, replication assets, and benchmark instructions. The rubric and judge-only addendum are hidden from the candidate.

Authors report random selection from the filtered candidate pool, followed by manual paper review and author recruitment. Main agent comparisons use three runs per model-paper pair where completed; exact random seed policy and the full candidate/rejection manifest are not released.

The paper reports 646 runs across its results. Main BasicAgent aims at six models x 20 papers x three runs; IterativeAgent evaluates three model/scaffold configurations, with extended runs and human baselines analyzed separately. The run-level corpus is not public.

Exclude papers with insufficient empirical engineering, multi-node compute, closed-source model dependencies, new human-data requirements, primary focus on frameworks/tools, inadequate reproducibility detail, or inaccessible/ fast-changing indispensable dependencies. A commercial/geographic affiliation filter is also applied before manual review.

Main agent attempts are capped at 12 hours on one A10 GPU; an o1 IterativeAgent experiment extends to 36 hours. Main-paper reproduction is capped at 12 hours. The agent receives Internet access and, where needed, Hugging Face and up to $1,000 in OpenAI API credit. Model token budgets and seeds are not fully stated.

No optimizer or policy-training stage is demonstrated. PaperBench is a capability evaluation and audit surface; using its hidden rubrics or judge scores for SFT/RL would be a new, unsupported protocol and would contaminate the public benchmark.

Twenty heterogeneous ICML 2024 papers across 12 topic areas, their full text, author clarifications, task-specific assets and dependencies, engineer/author rubrics, agent-generated repositories, clean-container execution evidence, and model-judge labels. Upstream datasets, pretrained models, APIs, and code rights vary by task and are not reconciled in one manifest.

The released all.txt contains the 20 public evaluation papers. Current dev.txt contains semantic-self-consistency, self-expansion, and self- composing-policies, whereas the ICML paper says two NeurIPS 2024 Workshop papers were released as development data. debug and testing are subsets of the public evaluation set, and a separate internal held-out set is mentioned but not described or released.

PaperBench selects contemporary papers rather than importing CORE-Bench, MLE-bench, MLAgentBench, or RE-Bench tasks, but no instance-, dependency-, or source-code-overlap audit is released. Public papers, rubrics, judge code, and benchmark assets create direct future evaluation-contamination risk.

Candidates cannot access listed author repositories or known online replications during a run, and agent logs are searched post hoc for blacklist URLs. The authors explicitly acknowledge that model pretraining may contain original paper/code information; no pretraining-contamination measurement, memorization probe, semantic overlap audit, or post-release exposure policy is reported.

The runtime is designed to store agent logs, status, metadata, timestamped submissions, initial/final/intermediate snapshots, reproduction outputs, and grades. Missing submissions and monitor violations score zero; reproduction or judge failures are counted in run-health fields. However runs/ is ignored and the official repository does not preserve the paper's complete successful, failed, timed-out, disqualified, and crashed run corpus for independent audit.

Partial at best. A pinned code commit and uv.lock help reconstruct the harness, and reproduction starts in a fresh container. Docker bases are tag- rather than digest-pinned; apt, get.docker.com, external datasets/APIs, credentials, agent-installed packages, hardware, seeds, and nondeterministic judge calls can drift. The original snapshots/submissions/judge outputs needed for record-and-replay are absent.

items: SimpleJudge obtains only the top ten files after model-based relevance ranking when a submission exceeds context, so relevant code or evidence can be omitted and create false negatives; file ranking is itself stochastic.

Result Match judging relies on newly modified whitelisted plaintext outputs and timestamps, which can miss binary checkpoints/images or reward crafted logs/tables that look plausible without scientifically valid replication.

JudgeEval contains only five submissions and reports o3-mini F1 0.83; it does not rule out paper-specific error, adversarial submissions, rubric loopholes, correlated leaf errors, or score drift under later judge models.

The blacklist monitor only flags normalized URLs near git clone, curl, or wget strings in recorded logs, so browser visits, Python HTTP clients, renamed mirrors, indirect package retrieval, omitted logs, and memorized code can evade the control.

Current reproduction salvaging may retry short runs under Python 3.11 and/or a new virtualenv; score comparability depends on recording which retry won, and this current default is not the same as the paper's single documented fresh-container protocol.

Large result archives can be truncated by current upload limits, model/API nondeterminism changes leaf grades, and a weighted average can award broad partial credit without successful end-to-end result reproduction.
Public rubrics, addenda, and judge implementation allow later agents to tune directly to the evaluation contract even though the runtime hides the rubric.
BasicAgent models frequently terminate early while claiming completion or an unsolved blocker.
Models can write multi-step plans without taking the tool actions needed to implement them.
o3-mini frequently struggles with tool use in the reported experiments.
Agent scores are much higher on Code Development than Execution or Result Match, so code volume does not imply reproduced findings.
Ten of 646 reported runs accessed blacklisted resources and were disqualified to zero.
Pretraining contamination from public papers and original repositories can inflate future scores.
The LLM judge is nondeterministic and not as accurate as expert human grading.
The current public dev split has three papers although the ICML paper describes two released development papers.
No complete paper-run trajectory/submission corpus supports training reuse or independent failure replay.

value.html: Benchmark tasks are based on public research artifacts rather than a disclosed collection of personal user data. Eight ML PhD participants provide the human baseline, but consent, compensation, IRB status, log retention, and withdrawal procedures are not reported. Human or agent run logs are not released, and no corpus-level privacy/redaction/takedown policy is published.

Reported agents receive unproxied Internet access, arbitrary shell/Python execution, package installation, an A10 GPU, Hugging Face credentials, and up to $1,000 in OpenAI API credit. Current setup uploads an agent.env file into the workspace and passes agent resource variables into reproduction. Secret isolation/redaction, network allowlists, egress monitoring, malicious package/ asset controls, Docker privilege boundaries, and incident handling are not documented as a benchmark-wide security policy.

frontier-evals is MIT licensed, but that notice does not by itself establish uniform rights for bundled paper PDFs/Markdown, author addenda, figures/assets, upstream datasets/models, agent outputs, or third-party repositories. The JudgeEval README gives specific attribution/permission notes and says some submission tarballs cannot be redistributed automatically, confirming that artifact rights require item-level review.

Public task folders and split files expose final paper IDs, source documents, addenda, rubrics, and blacklists. Missing are the full filtered ICML candidate pool, model-filter prompts/outputs, exclusion decisions, random-selection seed, author-contact/recruitment mapping, rubric revision/adjudication history, and immutable mapping from the 646 experiment runs to artifacts.
